hits.abstract: Large Language Model (LLM) collaborative decoding techniques improve output quality by combining the outputs of multiple models at each generation step, but they incur high computational costs. In this paper, we introduce Collaborative decoding via Speculation (CoS), a novel framework that accelerates collaborative decoding without compromising performance. Inspired by Speculative Decoding--where a small proposal model generates tokens sequentially, and a larger target model verifies them in parallel, our approach builds on two key insights: (1) the verification distribution can be the combined distribution of both the proposal and target models, and (2) alternating each model as the proposer and verifier can further enhance efficiency. We generalize this method to collaboration among n models and theoretically prove that CoS is never slower than standard collaborative decoding, typically achieving faster speed. Extensive experiments demonstrate CoS is 1.11x-2.23x faster than standard collaborative decoding without compromising generation quality. Our code is available at https://github.com/Kamichanw/CoS/.
hits.provider_summary: [research paper] CoS introduces a speculative decoding framework for collaborative LLM inference, generalizing speculative decoding to multi-model settings by leveraging combined distributions during verification and enabling alternating proposer-verifier roles to generate bonus tokens. The method reduces model invocations—achieving up to 2.23x speedup over standard collaborative decoding—while maintaining output quality through theoretical guarantees of non-degradation and provable acceptance rate bounds in weighted ensembles.
hits.title: Fast Large Language Model Collaborative Decoding via Speculation
